lines.text: A new teammate joins on Monday. Chen is smart, but has never seen your project.
Chen's agent knows nothing either. Not your conventions, and not the odd traps in your setup.
Normally, teammates spend weeks explaining it, one question at a time, in chat.
Instead, Chen accepts an invite link, and keeps their own account the whole time.
Then Chen shares a workspace with the team. Nothing is shared until each person chooses it.
Chen's agent reads the team memory, and learns, for example, that staging needs the VPN.
So it connects first, and skips the failure that has caught everyone else.
It picks up the team's skills, like release and deploy, wherever teammates chose to share them.
So Chen's first real task goes out before lunch, not after weeks of questions.
The team sees Chen's tasks as they happen, read-only, with Chen's name on each one.
The knowledge was already waiting for them, written down by the teammates who came before.
Onboard the agent with the team. Try it at Agent R Q dot com.
